senses.definition: to make something poorer in quality by adding another substance
senses.example: The milk had been adulterated with water.

senses.definition: to increase the power, status or wealth of
senses.example: The dictator used the war to aggrandize himself.

senses.definition: brisk and cheerful readiness
senses.example: She accepted the invitation with alacrity.

senses.definition: without guile or deception; natural and simple
senses.example: The child's artless questions made the adults laugh.

senses.definition: showing great care and perseverance
senses.example: Thanks to her assiduous research, the book is full of new detail.

senses.definition: to persuade someone to do something by sustained coaxing or flattery
senses.example: He cajoled his sister into lending him her car.

senses.definition: the quality of being open and honest; frankness
senses.example: The minister spoke with unusual candor about her mistakes.

senses.definition: to cause surprise or confusion in someone, especially by acting against their expectations
senses.example: The results confounded the experts.

senses.definition: to prove a theory or expectation wrong
senses.example: The underdogs confounded their critics by winning the league.

senses.definition: (of an atmosphere or event) friendly, lively and enjoyable
senses.example: The dinner was a convivial affair with plenty of laughter.

senses.definition: to reduce in extent or quantity; to impose a restriction on
senses.example: The budget cuts curtailed the museum's opening hours.

senses.definition: not influenced by considerations of personal advantage; impartial
senses.example: A disinterested referee settled the dispute.

senses.definition: to make known private or sensitive information
senses.example: The journalist refused to divulge her sources.

senses.definition: expressing feelings of gratitude, pleasure or approval in an unrestrained or heartfelt manner
senses.example: The critics were effusive in their praise.

senses.definition: to make something clear; to explain
senses.example: The appendix elucidates the methods used in the study.

senses.definition: to mention a number of things one by one
senses.example: The letter enumerates the reasons for the decision.

senses.definition: fair and impartial
senses.example: We want an equitable division of the profits.

senses.definition: to adopt or support a cause, belief or way of life
senses.example: In later life he espoused the cause of animal rights.

senses.definition: filled with or characterized by a lively energy and excitement
senses.example: The exuberant crowd danced in the streets.

senses.definition: growing profusely; lush
senses.example: The garden's exuberant growth needed weekly trimming.

senses.definition: well chosen or suited to the circumstances
senses.example: The book's title was a felicitous choice.

senses.definition: pleasing and fortunate
senses.example: The garden had a felicitous position by the river.

senses.definition: not showing a serious or respectful attitude
senses.example: His flippant reply to the judge earned him a fine.

senses.definition: (of words or a speaker) fluent and voluble but insincere and shallow
senses.example: The salesman had a glib answer for every objection.

senses.definition: easily persuaded to believe something; credulous
senses.example: Gullible investors lost millions in the scheme.

senses.definition: forbidden by law, rules or custom
senses.example: Police seized a shipment of illicit drugs.

senses.definition: to inspire or permeate with a feeling or quality
senses.example: Her speeches were imbued with a sense of urgency.

senses.definition: a situation in which no progress is possible, especially because of disagreement
senses.example: Talks reached an impasse over pay.

senses.definition: to bring about or initiate an action or event
senses.example: The new manager instigated a review of all spending.

senses.definition: to place or deal with close together for contrasting effect
senses.example: The exhibition juxtaposes old photographs with new ones of the same streets.

senses.definition: sumptuously rich, elaborate or luxurious
senses.example: They threw a lavish party for her fiftieth birthday.

senses.definition: to bestow something in generous or extravagant quantities upon
senses.example: The critics lavished praise on the young director.

senses.definition: a quality that evokes pity or sadness
senses.example: The play's final scene is full of pathos.

senses.definition: of secondary or minor importance; marginal
senses.example: The issue is peripheral to our main argument.

senses.definition: relating to or situated on the edge or periphery of something
senses.example: Peripheral vision helps us notice movement to the side.

senses.definition: to prolong
senses.example: The defense tried to protract the trial.

senses.definition: skill or expertise in a particular activity or field
senses.example: The boxer was famous for his prowess in the ring.

senses.definition: a state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation
senses.example: I'm in a quandary about which job to take.

senses.definition: to go back on a promise, undertaking or contract
senses.example: The buyer reneged on the deal at the last minute.

senses.definition: to express to someone one's disapproval of or disappointment in their actions
senses.example: She reproached him for forgetting her birthday.

senses.definition: the expression of disapproval or disappointment
senses.example: His conduct was beyond reproach.

senses.definition: involving or limited to basic principles
senses.example: He had only a rudimentary knowledge of French.

senses.definition: to think deeply about something
senses.example: She ruminated on the meaning of the dream.

senses.definition: having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; wise
senses.example: The sagacious old judge had seen it all before.

senses.definition: (of a person or process) diligent, thorough and extremely attentive to details
senses.example: The museum keeps scrupulous records of every loan.

senses.definition: very concerned to avoid doing wrong
senses.example: He was scrupulous about paying every debt.

senses.definition: (of a person) tending to spend much time seated; somewhat inactive
senses.example: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease.

senses.definition: the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation
senses.example: He sued his neighbor for slander.

senses.definition: to make false and damaging statements about someone
senses.example: She claimed that the paper had slandered her family.

senses.definition: the state of being sober
senses.example: He celebrated ten years of sobriety.

senses.definition: the quality of being staid or solemn
senses.example: The sobriety of the occasion called for dark suits.

senses.definition: to reject with disdain or contempt
senses.example: She spurned all offers of help.

senses.definition: very weak or slight
senses.example: The link between the two events is tenuous at best.

senses.definition: mentally or physically inactive; lethargic
senses.example: The heat made us torpid and sleepy.

senses.definition: a feeling of fear or agitation about something that may happen
senses.example: We approached the old bridge with trepidation.

senses.definition: a trace of something that is disappearing or no longer exists
senses.example: Not a vestige of the old castle remains.

senses.definition: (especially of a person or speech) vehement or clamorous
senses.example: The plan faced vociferous opposition from residents.

senses.definition: wanting or devouring great quantities of food
senses.example: Voracious caterpillars stripped the trees bare.

senses.definition: engaging in an activity with great eagerness or enthusiasm
senses.example: She was a voracious reader as a child.

senses.definition: the time at which something is most powerful or successful
senses.example: The empire reached its zenith in the second century.

senses.definition: the point in the sky directly above an observer
senses.example: At noon the sun stood near its zenith.
